recentItems.title: Why thousands of protesters blocked Orange Order march in Northern Ireland
recentItems.description:
Thousands of protesters have blocked a controversial loyalist Orange Order march from going ahead on a Catholic street in Northern Ireland for the first time in nearly 30 years.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

A late-night legal ruling authorised the march along Garvaghy Road in Portadown - a location renowned as a major Troubles flashpoint in the 1990s.

recentItems.title: Counter terror police investigating major incident at RAF Fairford base
recentItems.description:
Counter terrorism police are leading an investigation into a major incident near an RAF base in Gloucestershire used in American attacks against Iran. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Five men were arrested in the early hours of Sunday morning near RAF Fairford, on suspicion of committing offences under the Explosives Act, while 85 homes in the nearby village of Whelford were also evacuated.

recentItems.title: Burnham's first Labour conference as prime minister
recentItems.description:
Andy Burnham is gearing up for his first Labour Party conference as prime minister.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The slogan for this year's annual gathering is "Hope Again" - and on Tuesday in his main speech Andy Burnham will set out how he intends to deliver change to Britain. 

But there are disagreements within the cabinet on a number of issues including care worker visas, and immigration.

recentItems.title: What could Man City punishment be over alleged financial breaches?
recentItems.description:
Manchester City continues to protest its innocence - but it seems to have gone beyond the point where anyone is actually listening.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Found in breach of more than 100 financial regulations, all the questions now are what the punishment will be? 

And what does it all mean not just for one disgraced football club but for football itself?

The former Kings of Europe find their crown sullied by breaches across nearly fifteen seasons. 

Could other premier league teams who played against them during those years cry foul and seek damages for games they may now argue were not fairly played?
